transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-02 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes | Attendees: Maya Chen, Carlos Rivera (Redwood); Jordan Blake, Priya Kaur, Samir Patel (SignalWave)

Summary: Quick renewal check-in focused on committed capacity increase, onboarding two additional regions (eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1), and aligning on contract extension length and security paperwork. Agreed to run private benchmarks and follow up with revised SOW.

Topics: capacity planning, regional rollout, contract extension, security/KMS, performance SLAs, billing/commit model, next steps.

00:00:02 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
00:00:07 Jordan Blake: Yeah, loud and clear. Thanks for setting this up.
00:00:12 Priya Kaur: Hi, thanks. We've got about 45 minutes if that works.
00:00:18 Maya Chen: Perfect. Quick agenda — one, renewal mechanics; two, capacity bump; three, region onboarding and security; four, next steps. Carlos from our infra team will cover the benchmarks.
00:00:31 Carlos Rivera: Hey all. I'll try to keep it light — main ask is figures for peak qps and tail-latency targets so we can size Dedicated pools.
00:00:42 Samir Patel: From procurement perspective, timeline is important — we need final commercial terms by early next week to sync with finance.
00:00:52 Jordan Blake: Right. Current usage has been steady: 180k tokens/day average, spikes to ~650k during batch jobs. We've been happy with the Dedicated performance but need better predictability across EU and APAC.
00:01:10 Maya Chen: Got it. When you say predictability, do you mean capacity in-region or latency SLAs or both?
00:01:18 Jordan Blake: Both. Latency for inference in eu should be sub-120ms p95 for our 1k-token sequences, and in APAC we need similar numbers otherwise user experience drops.
00:01:30 Carlos Rivera: Those are reasonable. For 1k sequences, p95 at <120ms typically needs local GPU pools plus aggressive prefix caching and batching tuning. We can do that with Dedicated in-region pools and a small reserve for burst.
00:01:45 Priya Kaur: How much extra capacity are we talking about? Our usage pattern is spiky but predictable around business hours.
00:01:53 Carlos Rivera: Based on the numbers you just shared, we'd recommend a 20% committed bump to start, plus a burst buffer that covers ~2x your current spike qps — that keeps your effective latency SLO without overcommitting spend.
00:02:10 Jordan Blake: 20% seems fair as a starting point. We're also planning to onboard eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 in Q4, and we'd like region-specific commitments rather than a global pool, for data residency reasons.
00:02:24 Maya Chen: Totally understood. We can split committed capacity by region in the SOW. We'll need to confirm KMS and data residency controls for the private control plane if you go with Private or VPC deployment.
00:02:37 Priya Kaur: Security is critical. We'll need SOC 2 plus proof of key management — HSM or customer-managed KMS. Also audit log retention for 13 months.
00:02:48 Carlos Rivera: We support customer KMS integrations and can provide SOC 2 artifacts. Audit logs retention is configurable, we can map that into the Private offering or even Dedicated with VPC peering depending on your preference.
00:02:59 Samir Patel: On contract length — finance prefers 12 months to align with fiscal planning, but we are open to 24 months if pricing improvement is meaningful.
00:03:10 Maya Chen: Short answer: we can do a 12-month extension with a 20% committed increase, or 24 months with an additional discount tier. I'll include both options in the SOW.
00:03:22 Jordan Blake: Can you outline the discount band for 24 months now? Even a ballpark helps for our internal discussions.
00:03:28 Maya Chen: Ballpark: an incremental ~8-12% off unit rate for a 24-month commit versus 12-month. Exact depends on region splits.
00:03:38 Priya Kaur: Understood. Back to performance — are there any model variants or quantization options we should consider? We prefer to keep quality but willing to test int8 if cost savings are large.
00:03:52 Carlos Rivera: We can test quantized variants in the benchmark. For many of the open models we support int8/4 and can measure quality delta. Our Optimize recommendations will include quantization and batching suggestions.
00:04:06 Jordan Blake: Great. Can Redwood run the benchmark in our accounts or you need access?
00:04:12 Carlos Rivera: We can run in your VPC if you prefer — that'll show end-to-end. Alternatively we can run in Redwood Dedicated in the target region with synthetic ingress to simulate your traffic. Running in your VPC gives better fidelity for networking and KMS.
00:04:26 Priya Kaur: We prefer VPC-run so we can validate KMS flows. We'll need a step-by-step runbook.
00:04:32 Carlos Rivera: We'll share the runbook and a small test harness; I'll set up a two-hour window for the full run.
00:04:38 Samir Patel: On billing, how are overages handled with committed capacity plus burst? We want predictable invoicing.
00:04:45 Maya Chen: Overage policy is in the SOW. Typically bursts beyond the buffer are billed at a higher unit rate, with monthly reconciliation. We can also propose a smoothing mechanism (billing credit) for planned seasonal spikes.
00:04:58 Jordan Blake: That could work. Also, we had an incident last quarter when a cache miss caused a large spike; are there guardrails to auto-fallback to a lower-cost model variant in emergencies?
00:05:09 Carlos Rivera: Yes, routing policies support automated fallback to compatible variants or to a higher-latency but lower-cost tier. We can configure canary rules and A/B rollouts so you don't lose availability.
00:05:21 Priya Kaur: For APAC region — what's typical lead time for Dedicated GPU pools?
00:05:26 Carlos Rivera: Usually 2-4 weeks for initial provisioning in an existing cloud region, shorter if you accept shared staging capacity. For Private on-prem it's longer.
00:05:36 Jordan Blake: Ok. We want the eu provisioned first, then apac a week later ideally.
00:05:42 Maya Chen: Noted. We'll propose timeline in SOW: eu-west-1 week-of-2026-10-10; ap-southeast-1 week-of-2026-10-17 subject to final sign-off.
00:05:53 Samir Patel: Good. Any legal red flags to call out? Data residency clause and indemnities?
00:05:58 Maya Chen: We typically include a data processing addendum for EU residency and can work with your counsel on indemnities. We'll surface any contract amendments in the SOW draft.
00:06:08 Jordan Blake: Can you also include a clause for performance regression monitoring — like rollbacks if quality drops after an update?
00:06:15 Carlos Rivera: We have Canary + automatic rollback and quality monitors linked to your eval prompt sets. We'll document alert thresholds and SLAs.
00:06:23 Priya Kaur: On the SOC 2 artifacts — can Redwood provide recent report and a contact for audits?
00:06:30 Maya Chen: Yes, we'll attach the SOC 2 Type II and security contact.
00:06:34 Jordan Blake: Quick note — our legal team wants a clause about encryption in transit and at rest, and confirmation that metadata won't be used for model training.
00:06:43 Maya Chen: We already have a clause: Redwood does not use customer content to train models and supports encryption at rest/in transit with customer KMS. We'll include formal language.
00:06:52 Samir Patel: Fantastic. Anything else on pricing structure? We want committed qps broken down by route (ingest vs embedding).
00:07:00 Maya Chen: Please send the route breakdown; Jordan, you mentioned endpoints and qps per region — if we get that, we can map to committed units and per-route cost.
00:07:08 Jordan Blake: I'll send those after this call.
00:07:11 Carlos Rivera: For the benchmark, do you have a representative prompt set and evals? That will help measure quality impact if we try int8.
00:07:20 Jordan Blake: Yes, I'll share a sanitized prompt set and the eval scripts. Expect to remove PII.
00:07:26 Maya Chen: Great. So recap: we'll draft SOW with 12-month and 24-month options, include region splits, SOC 2 and KMS language, and benchmark plan. Carlos will run private benchmarks and share runbook. Jordan will send qps and prompt set. Samir needs commercial terms by next week.
00:07:44 Priya Kaur: Sounds good. One more question — support SLA for P1 incidents?
00:07:49 Maya Chen: Standard enterprise SLA with 1-hour initial response for P1 and four-hour mitigation target; we can elevate to tighter windows with premium SLA add-on.
00:07:59 Samir Patel: We'll evaluate the SLA add-on.
00:08:03 Jordan Blake: Anything else?
00:08:05 Maya Chen: No, that's it from us. Thanks for the time. We'll send materials.
00:08:10 Carlos Rivera: I'll follow up on the benchmark schedule and test harness link.
00:08:14 Jordan Blake: Thanks everyone.
00:08:16 Priya Kaur: Thanks.
00:08:18 Samir Patel: Bye.
